title: Progress towards measles and rubella elimination in Lesotho, 2011–2025

analysis.scope_and_question: Since 1996, the country has been implementing measles elimination strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This included Lesotho's annual WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for routine measles-containing vaccine (MCV) doses; performance in the periodic measles rubella vaccination campaigns and case-based surveillance; and the trends of measles and rubella incidences.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MCV2 coverage reached 80% in 2011 and 2012 before declining in subsequent years.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not clearly state controversies or evidence gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: To sustain the gains made, the country should work to strengthen vaccination in the second year of life, reinforce demand generation during preventive campaigns, address population denominator inaccuracies that hinder accurate coverage tracking, and systematically document measles and rubella virus genotypes.

analysis.summary_en: Since 1996, the country has been implementing measles elimination strategies. This included Lesotho's annual WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for routine measles-containing vaccine (MCV) doses; performance in the periodic measles rubella vaccination campaigns and case-based surveillance; and the trends of measles and rubella incidences. MCV2 coverage reached 80% in 2011 and 2012 before declining in subsequent years. The supplied evidence does not clearly state controversies or evidence gaps. To sustain the gains made, the country should work to strengthen vaccination in the second year of life, reinforce demand generation during preventive campaigns, address population denominator inaccuracies that hinder accurate coverage tracking, and systematically document measles and rubella virus genotypes.

title: Deterministic and ANN-based modelling of measles transmission using real epidemiological data

analysis.research_question_and_background: The qualitative properties of the model, including positivity and boundedness of solutions, are established.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aims to develop a nonlinear SVLIQR epidemic model to investigate measles transmission dynamics by incorporating vaccination, latency, quarantine, and treatment effects.
analysis.methods: In addition, model parameters are estimated using the least squares method based on reported measles cases in China from 2005 to 2017.
analysis.main_results: The results show that the model fits the reported data well, and the ANN framework provides highly accurate and convergent approximations under different epidemiological parameter settings.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Overall, the proposed framework provides a useful and reliable tool for understanding measles dynamics and assessing effective intervention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Numerical simulations further indicate that higher vaccination and quarantine rates significantly reduce measles transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: To improve the numerical approximation and capture the nonlinear dynamics of the system, an ANN-based solver coupled with the ode45 scheme is implemented.

analysis.summary_en: The qualitative properties of the model, including positivity and boundedness of solutions, are established. This study aims to develop a nonlinear SVLIQR epidemic model to investigate measles transmission dynamics by incorporating vaccination, latency, quarantine, and treatment effects. In addition, model parameters are estimated using the least squares method based on reported measles cases in China from 2005 to 2017. The results show that the model fits the reported data well, and the ANN framework provides highly accurate and convergent approximations under different epidemiological parameter settings. Overall, the proposed framework provides a useful and reliable tool for understanding measles dynamics and assessing effective intervention strategies. Numerical simulations further indicate that higher vaccination and quarantine rates significantly reduce measles transmission. To improve the numerical approximation and capture the nonlinear dynamics of the system, an ANN-based solver coupled with the ode45 scheme is implemented.

title: A longitudinal study on how trust shapes psychological reactance to the German measles vaccine mandate

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the psychological effects of a measles vaccine mandate on public acceptance and vaccine uptake, addressing the underexplored area of psychological reactance in vaccine mandates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal online survey was conducted with 6901 respondents, including parents affected by the mandate and adults without children, over 20 months from August 2020 to March 2022.
analysis.methods: Multilevel modeling and logistic regression were used to analyze the temporal development of reactance, group differences, and the role of trust in mandate acceptance.
analysis.main_results: Reactance levels were low and stable over time, while attitudes toward the mandate became increasingly negative. Higher trust was associated with lower reactance and more positive attitudes, and higher initial reactance predicted a lower likelihood of later voluntary vaccine uptake.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that reactance to public health policies may persist and influence downstream health behavior, highlighting the importance of building trust and effective enforcement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform public health strategies to mitigate opposition to vaccine mandates and promote vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on self-reported data and the lack of randomization may limit the generalizability of the findings, but the multilevel modeling approach provides robust insights into the temporal dynamics of reactance.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined the psychological reactance to a measles vaccine mandate in Germany, finding that reactance levels were stable but attitudes became increasingly negative. Higher trust was associated with lower reactance and more positive attitudes, and initial reactance predicted lower voluntary vaccine uptake. These findings suggest that reactance may persist and influence health behavior, emphasizing the need for trust-building and effective enforcement.

title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Life-Threatening Measles in Children: A Case Series

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine whether extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is feasible in children with measles, addressing the resurgent global measles threat and severe disease progression to cardiorespiratory failure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with a regional ECMO program, involving 49 children younger than 18 years with laboratory-confirmed measles who received ECMO during the August 2025-May 2026 outbreak.
analysis.methods: The study involved a retrospective analysis of all children with measles who received ECMO, including indications for ECMO, type of ECMO used, and patient characteristics such as age, sex, and vaccination status.
analysis.main_results: Of 49 children with measles, 10 received ECMO. The survival rate was 60%, with complications including bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concluded that ECMO was feasible and potentially lifesaving in measles-associated cardiorespiratory failure, with survival comparable to other high-acuity pediatric indications, but the course was complicated by bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority, as these resource-intensive presentations occurred exclusively in unvaccinated children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, and the generalizability of the findings may be restricted to similar settings with access to ECMO programs.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the feasibility of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in children with measles. Of 49 children with measles, 10 received ECMO, with a 60% survival rate. Complications included bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury. The findings highlight the importance of measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority.

title: Seroprotection after measles vaccination in children with sickle cell anemia receiving hydroxyurea

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether children with sickle cell anemia (SCA) receiving hydroxyurea have adequate seroprotection after measles vaccination, addressing a knowledge gap about vaccine effectiveness in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on children with SCA enrolled in the TREAT trial to assess antimeasles seroprotection following first and second measles vaccinations.
analysis.methods: Seroprotection was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to detect immunoglobulin G (IgG) levels of ≥200 IU/L after first (MV1) and second (MV2) measles vaccinations.
analysis.main_results: Seroprotection was achieved by 33 of 35 children (94%) after MV1 and by 46 of 50 (92%) after MV2. Each additional year of age at MV2 was associated with decreased odds of seroprotection (OR, 0.25; P = .02). Earlier hydroxyurea initiation was linked to increased seroprotection (OR, 4.4; P = .02).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that most children with SCA are adequately protected after measles vaccination, similar to the general population, and that timely vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment are associated with increased seroprotection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the importance of timely measles vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment in ensuring adequate seroprotection among children with SCA, which is critical for public health strategies in regions with high SCA prevalence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and clear statistical associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated measles vaccine effectiveness in children with sickle cell anemia (SCA) receiving hydroxyurea. It found that 94% of children achieved seroprotection after the first dose and 92% after the second. Age at vaccination was inversely associated with seroprotection, while earlier hydroxyurea initiation was linked to higher protection. These results suggest that timely vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment are important for ensuring adequate measles immunity in SCA patients, which has implications for public health strategies in areas with high SCA prevalence. The study's retrospective design and potential confounding factors limit its generalizability, but the large sample size and clear statistical associations support its findings.

title: Timeliness of measles vaccination in selected districts of Oromia Region, Ethiopia – 2021

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background Delays in vaccination with the first/s dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1, MCV2) increases risk of measles transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Methods A secondary analysis from a 2021 cross-sectional household survey of children aged 12–35 months in Oromia, Ethiopia was conducted.
analysis.methods: Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression, with urban/rural stratification.
analysis.main_results: Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination differed in urban and rural areas, but common themes included increased caregiver immunization awareness and service delivery aspects.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Conclusions Although most children who received MCV1 were vaccinated by 12 months, many received delayed doses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: MCV2 coverage was low, irrespective of vaccination timing.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Among vaccinated children, the proportion receiving early, timely, and delayed doses was 30.1%, 44.5%, and 25.3% for MCV1, and 28.6%, 41.2%, and 30.3% for MCV2, respectively.

analysis.summary_en: Background Delays in vaccination with the first/s dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1, MCV2) increases risk of measles transmission. Methods A secondary analysis from a 2021 cross-sectional household survey of children aged 12–35 months in Oromia, Ethiopia was conducted. Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression, with urban/rural stratification. Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination differed in urban and rural areas, but common themes included increased caregiver immunization awareness and service delivery aspects. Conclusions Although most children who received MCV1 were vaccinated by 12 months, many received delayed doses. MCV2 coverage was low, irrespective of vaccination timing. Among vaccinated children, the proportion receiving early, timely, and delayed doses was 30.1%, 44.5%, and 25.3% for MCV1, and 28.6%, 41.2%, and 30.3% for MCV2, respectively.

title: Measles and Rubella Surveillance in the Digital Era

analysis.scope_and_question: The scope and question focus on the evolution of measles and rubella surveillance in the digital era, specifically examining the integration of digital technologies in surveillance methods and their impact on scientific output and thematic trends.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilized a bibliometric analysis of 154 articles published between 1990 and 2026, conducted using the Scopus database and the R package Bibliometrix. The study aimed to map the scientific literature on measles and rubella surveillance in the digital era, identifying trends and thematic clusters.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that scientific output increased progressively, with a peak in 2025. The thematic analysis revealed three major clusters: epidemiological surveillance, vaccination strategies, and the integration of digital health systems. The review also highlighted the growing prominence of genomic surveillance and digital health systems, emphasizing the need for deeper integration of AI methods.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review noted that earlier research mainly focused on conventional surveillance and public health, while recent publications emphasized digital and genomic surveillance. There is a need for more research on the integration of AI methods to strengthen early outbreak detection and real-time vaccination monitoring.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on deepening the integration of AI methods in surveillance systems to enhance early detection and monitoring of outbreaks. Practical implications include the need for improved real-time vaccination monitoring and support for international elimination goals.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the evolution of measles and rubella surveillance in the digital era, highlighting the increasing prominence of genomic surveillance and digital health systems. It emphasizes the need for deeper integration of AI methods to strengthen early outbreak detection and real-time vaccination monitoring.

title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case

analysis.research_question_and_background: The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population.
analysis.methods: This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity.
analysis.main_results: Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

analysis.summary_en: The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

title: Factors Associated with Up-to-Date Measles Vaccination Among 2-Year-Old Children in Canada: An Analysis of the 2021 Childhood National Immunization Coverage Survey

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify factors associated with up-to-date measles vaccination among 2-year-olds in Canada, addressing the ongoing importance of examining predictors of measles vaccination due to measles outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used national cross-sectional data from the 2021 Childhood National Immunization Coverage Survey (cNICS) conducted among 2-year-old Canadian children between January 2022 and July 2022.
analysis.methods: The study examined proportions of vaccinated children by sociodemographic characteristics and conducted multivariable logistic regression analysis to determine factors associated with up-to-date measles vaccination coverage.
analysis.main_results: Among 3118 two-year-olds, 91.6% (95% CI: 89.9–93.1) were up-to-date with their measles vaccines. Lower odds of being up-to-date were associated with a household income of less than $60,000, experiencing pandemic-related obstacles, and parental hesitancy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that lower household income, experiencing pandemic-related obstacles, and parental hesitancy contribute to being not up-to-date on measles vaccination among children in Canada, highlighting the need for targeted programs and communication efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the development of targeted programs and communication efforts to increase measles vaccination coverage in Canada, addressing the ongoing importance of measles vaccination due to outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the potential for self-reported data to introduce bias. The evidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined factors associated with up-to-date measles vaccination among 2-year-olds in Canada, finding that lower household income, pandemic-related obstacles, and parental hesitancy were associated with lower vaccination rates. The findings support targeted programs to increase coverage.

title: Progress and Barriers Define the Journey to Measles Elimination in Africa

analysis.scope_and_question: Measles virus (Morbillivirus hominis), historical taxonomic names, rubeola and measles disease. Biologically related animal, taxonomic, model, differential-diagnosis and comparative entities are supplementary-only unless material target-specific evidence is also present; only explicit lexical or unrelated hard exclusions are terminal.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A review of approximately 252 sources (2016 2025) from PubMed and WHO/UNICEF databases using the Boolean strategy was done. Sixty-five articles were selected and thematically synthesised to gather evidence via a four-domain framework (epidemiology, health resilience, innovations, and socio-cultural factors).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Measles remains one of the most contagious and deadly childhood diseases. The objective of this review was to examine recent epidemiological evidence on measles elimination progress and barriers in Africa towards the WHO’s 2030 goal and to identify scalable strategies through a holistic analysis of epidemiological, systems, innovation, and socio cultural aspects. From 2017 to 2021, measles incidence in Africa rose from 69.2 to 81.9 cases per million. Coverage of measles-containing vaccine was 69% and 41% for the first and second doses, respectively, falling far below the 95% herd immunity threshold. Key barriers included weak health systems, vaccine hesitancy, COVID-19 disruptions, and cross-border transmission.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The search query used was (measles OR "measles virus") AND (epidemiology OR "vaccination coverage" OR elimination OR outbreaks OR barriers OR innovations) AND (Africa). Case studies show Rwanda sustained >95% for the first dose of measles-containing vaccine via digital systems, and the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak in 2018-2020 resulted in 458,000 cases and 8,000 deaths.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Innovations included drone delivery of vaccine, District Health Information System 2/Short Message Service reminders, thermostable microarray patches, and genomic surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the progress and barriers in measles elimination in Africa, focusing on the measles virus and its impact on public health. Despite over 50 years of vaccine availability, Africa continues to bear a disproportionate burden of measles, with incidence rising from 69.2 to 81.9 cases per million between 2017 and 2021. Vaccine coverage remains low, with only 69% and 41% for the first and second doses, respectively, far below the 95% threshold needed for herd immunity. Key barriers include weak health systems, vaccine hesitancy, disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, and cross-border transmission. The review highlights innovations such as drone delivery, digital reminders, thermostable patches, and genomic surveillance as potential tools to improve vaccination rates and control outbreaks. Case studies from Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo illustrate both successes and challenges in achieving measles elimination. Integrated strategies involving resilient systems, regional collaboration, domestic funding, and community engagement are emphasized as essential for closing immunity gaps and meeting the WHO's 2030 elimination goal.

title: A Multiscale Dynamical-Systems Model of Measles Immuno-Epidemiology with ODE-to-Cellular-Automaton Coupling

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a multiscale mathematical framework that couples within-host viral dynamics with population-level epidemiological modeling to better understand measles virus transmission and its impact on host populations. The background highlights the complexity of measles virus infection, which involves nonlinear processes across biological scales.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multiscale mathematical framework was developed by coupling a seven-variable within-host ordinary differential equation model to a stochastic cellular automaton. The study simulated population-level dynamics using six host archetypes as structured parameter perturbations of the common dynamical core.
analysis.methods: The within-host system extended a four-variable measles immunodynamics core by incorporating IFN-γ-dominant and IL-17-associated immune responses, persistent viral RNA, and neutralizing antibodies. The framework included an explicit ODE-to-cellular-automaton map that translated within-host trajectories into infectious timing, daily infectivity profiles, and severity-to-death transition mappings.
analysis.main_results: Population simulations demonstrated a nonlinear reduction in attack rate with increasing vaccination coverage, reduced modeled death burden under targeted high-risk in silico perturbations, and additional suppression under reactive vaccination campaigns. A direct local cellular-automaton secondary-infection estimate was reported instead of interpreting cumulative infectivity burden as a reproduction number.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the importance of cross-scale coupling in capturing the nonlinear dynamics of measles virus transmission. The novelty lies in the explicit cross-scale coupling operator that separates ODE-derived host descriptors from epidemiological mapping rules.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The framework provides a tool for understanding how within-host viral dynamics influence population-level transmission and mortality, which can inform more accurate surveillance, risk assessment, and vaccination strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on in silico perturbations and the assumption of population-level contact and susceptibility. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are based on mathematical modeling rather than empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a multiscale mathematical framework that couples within-host measles virus dynamics with population-level stochastic cellular automaton models. The framework incorporates nonlinear processes such as immune-cell depletion, persistent viral RNA, and vaccination-dependent spread. By extending the traditional four-variable immunodynamics model to include IFN-γ and IL-17 responses, the study captures within-host heterogeneity and its impact on population-level outcomes. The results show a nonlinear reduction in attack rates with increased vaccination coverage and highlight the importance of targeted high-risk perturbations and reactive vaccination campaigns in reducing mortality. The authors emphasize that the framework's explicit cross-scale coupling operator allows for transparent propagation of within-host dynamics into spatial stochastic models, offering new insights into measles transmission. However, the study's reliance on in silico simulations and assumptions about population-level contact and susceptibility limits its empirical validation. The findings suggest potential applications in improving surveillance, risk assessment, and vaccination strategies, but the evidence is moderate due to the model-based nature of the results.

title: The 2026 Measles Outbreak in Bangladesh: A Critique of Immunity Gaps and Care Deficiencies

analysis.research_question_and_background: Bangladesh entered 2026 amid a severe measles outbreak that peaked in mid-May, prompting an analysis of the public health response and government management of the crisis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluates the public health response to the 2026 measles outbreak in Bangladesh, focusing on the government's management of the crisis.
analysis.methods: Health professionals and measles experts attributed the outbreak to accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
analysis.main_results: The study identifies accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding as contributing factors to the outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the outbreak as a result of systemic failures in immunisation and public health infrastructure, highlighting the novel intersection of nutritional deficiencies and measles vulnerability in the Bangladeshi context.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for strengthened routine immunisation programmes, improved public health infrastructure, and targeted nutritional interventions to prevent future measles outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on expert attributions without primary data collection or statistical analysis, limiting causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This study critiques the 2026 measles outbreak in Bangladesh, attributing it to gaps in routine immunisation, weak public health infrastructure, and nutritional deficiencies among children and mothers. The analysis evaluates the government's response, highlighting systemic failures in managing the crisis. The findings underscore the need for strengthened immunisation programmes, improved healthcare infrastructure, and targeted nutritional interventions to prevent future outbreaks. The evidence is moderate in strength, relying on expert attributions without primary data.

title: Association Between Caregiver Measles Vaccine Hesitancy and Incomplete Measles Rubella Immunization Among Children Aged 15–59 Months: A Multicenter Cross Sectional Study in Chattogram Division, Bangladesh

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aims to assess the association between caregiver measles vaccine hesitancy and incomplete measles rubella immunization among children aged 15–59 months. The research is motivated by the need to understand factors contributing to vaccine hesitancy and its impact on immunization completion.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter hospital based cross sectional study will be conducted in three tertiary government medical college hospitals in Chattogram Division, Bangladesh, recruiting 513 caregiver child pairs using consecutive sampling.
analysis.methods: Caregiver vaccine hesitancy will be assessed using a structured questionnaire, while measles rubella (MR1 and MR2) vaccination status will be determined from caregiver responses and verified using vaccination cards, immunization records, or institutional records.
analysis.main_results: The study will examine sociodemographic, behavioral, and healthcare related factors associated with vaccine hesitancy and incomplete measles rubella immunization, but no specific results are reported in the provided evidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding these factors could contribute to addressing vaccine hesitancy, but no explicit novel findings are stated in the provided evidence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could inform strategies to improve measles rubella immunization rates by addressing caregiver hesitancy, though no specific implications are detailed in the provided evidence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the evidence is based on caregiver-reported data, which may introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between caregiver measles vaccine hesitancy and incomplete measles rubella immunization among children aged 15–59 months in Chattogram Division, Bangladesh. Conducted as a multicenter cross-sectional study, it recruits caregiver-child pairs from three hospitals using consecutive sampling. The methods involve structured questionnaires and verification of vaccination status through records. The study will explore sociodemographic, behavioral, and healthcare factors influencing vaccine hesitancy and immunization completion. While the authors suggest that understanding these factors could aid in improving immunization rates, no specific results or novel findings are reported. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on caregiver-reported data introduce limitations, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Insights on United States cumulative measles cases during the 2026 outbreak using ARIMA and generalized linear models

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the nature of the 2026 measles outbreaks in the United States by analyzing historical surveillance data using four distinct forecasting models. The research addressed the need to adapt public health tracking to the heightened risk environment and the potential for a substantial increase in case burden compared to previous years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used historical surveillance data from 1997 to 2026, focusing on cumulative measles cases. The design involved four forecasting models: count-regression models (Poisson, quasi-Poisson, and negative binomial), and an ARIMAX model. The study evaluated the models' performance using out-of-sample validation data from May 1, 2026.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed cumulative measles cases using count-regression models and an ARIMAX model. The count-regression models incorporated outbreak-related covariates to capture persistent shifts in cumulative disease burden, while the ARIMAX model combined outbreak indicators with temporal dependence. The models were evaluated using a grid search approach, and the final selected model was ARIMAX(2,0,0).
analysis.main_results: The 2026 validation dataset consisted of cumulative measles cases reported through May 1, 2026. The study found that the final 2026 case burden would substantially exceed previous years, and forecasts were accompanied by 95% prediction intervals to quantify uncertainty.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provided a practical assessment of the suitability of different forecasting approaches for predicting cumulative measles burden in the post-elimination United States. The selected models offered formal uncertainty quantification, which is essential for public-health decision making.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings supported epidemiological surveillance, outbreak monitoring, and evidence-based public health decision-making. The study highlighted the need for adapting public health tracking to the heightened risk environment and the potential for a substantial increase in case burden.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations included the small number of annual observations, which made highly parameterized machine-learning approaches difficult to estimate reliably. The evidence strength was moderate due to the reliance on historical data and the need for continuous updates to the surveillance data.

analysis.summary_en: The study analyzed historical surveillance data from 1997 to 2026 to understand the 2026 measles outbreaks in the United States using four forecasting models. The ARIMAX(2,0,0) model was selected, and the study found that the 2026 case burden would substantially exceed previous years, emphasizing the need for public health adaptation.

title: Separating the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine could decrease access for Colorado parents

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the uncertainty among Colorado parents regarding vaccine safety and necessity, particularly the MMR vaccine. The background highlights parents' desire for vaccine customization and the potential impact of recent executive orders on vaccine access and choice.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study design involves qualitative research, including interviews with Colorado parents, pediatricians, researchers, and policymakers, as well as observations of vaccine clinics and educational events.
analysis.methods: The methods include qualitative data collection through interviews and observations, with no specific laboratory or statistical procedures mentioned.
analysis.main_results: The main results show that parents in Colorado value vaccine customization, with some opting for fewer injections or specific vaccines based on perceived risks. The study also reports an increase in vaccine exemptions in Colorado since the pandemic, with lower vaccination rates compared to the national average.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that parents' concerns about vaccine safety and customization are significant, and that recent executive orders may inadvertently complicate vaccine access. The novelty lies in the detailed insights into parents' decision-making processes and the challenges they face.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against policies that may limit vaccine access or complicate the decision-making process for parents, emphasizing the need for clear and consistent public health information.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include its qualitative nature and the potential for selection bias in the sample of parents interviewed. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of quantitative data and the focus on parental perspectives.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores parental concerns about vaccine safety and customization in Colorado, highlighting the challenges of recent executive orders on vaccine access. Qualitative research shows that parents value vaccine choice and customization, with some opting for fewer injections or specific vaccines based on perceived risks. The findings suggest that policies should consider the practical and logistical challenges faced by parents and healthcare providers.

analysis.summary_en: If you’re exposed to measles If you are vaccinated or have had measles, there is little risk – about 3% – that you will develop measles if exposed to the virus. Francis coordinated the entire polio vaccine field trial, which included 1.8 million children, and deemed the polio vaccine “safe, effective, potent.” As of Sept. That compares with 16 cases statewide in all of 2025. each year, 48,000 were hospitalized, and as many as 500 died. Allegheny County reported its first case tied to the current outbreak in August, when the county health department warned of a potential exposure at UPMC Children’s Hospital’s emergency department. The current measles outbreak could be a test of whether the local history still means something for vaccination rates today. But there is an added bonus: When the majority of a population is vaccinated, there are community-wide effects, mainly that community transmission of measles will begin to decline.

title: Clinical Spectrum and Electroencephalographic Correlation in Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis: A Case Series

analysis.research_question_and_background: Characterized by cognitive deterioration, behavioral abnormalities, progressive motor deficit, and stereotyped slow myoclonic jerks, its clinical hallmarks are intricately linked to classic electroencephalographic (EEG) periodic slow-wave complexes (Radermecker complexes).
analysis.study_design_and_population: Case Presentation: We report a series of four distinct clinical presentations of SSPE Case 1 describes a 20-year-old male with initial focal myoclonic seizures, asymmetric hemiparesis, cognitive decline, subsequent progression to generalized myoclonus, and typical generalized Radermecker complexes post-intrathecal interferon-alpha therapy.
analysis.methods: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the core experimental, analytical, or statistical methods.
analysis.main_results: Case 4 outlines an atypical, protracted decade-long course in a 20-year-old male misdiagnosed with primary psychiatric illness and movement disorders before presenting with severe cognitive failure, gait cessation, and classic periodic discharges.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Discussion & Conclusion: These cases demonstrate the broad phenotypic spectrum of SSPE-spanning classic juvenile presentation, focal onset, neurosurgical confounders, and protracted psychiatric-extrapyramidal masquerades.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The supplied evidence does not clearly state a specific scientific or public-health implication.

analysis.summary_en: Characterized by cognitive deterioration, behavioral abnormalities, progressive motor deficit, and stereotyped slow myoclonic jerks, its clinical hallmarks are intricately linked to classic electroencephalographic (EEG) periodic slow-wave complexes (Radermecker complexes). Case Presentation: We report a series of four distinct clinical presentations of SSPE Case 1 describes a 20-year-old male with initial focal myoclonic seizures, asymmetric hemiparesis, cognitive decline, subsequent progression to generalized myoclonus, and typical generalized Radermecker complexes post-intrathecal interferon-alpha therapy. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the core experimental, analytical, or statistical methods. Case 4 outlines an atypical, protracted decade-long course in a 20-year-old male misdiagnosed with primary psychiatric illness and movement disorders before presenting with severe cognitive failure, gait cessation, and classic periodic discharges. Discussion & Conclusion: These cases demonstrate the broad phenotypic spectrum of SSPE-spanning classic juvenile presentation, focal onset, neurosurgical confounders, and protracted psychiatric-extrapyramidal masquerades. The supplied evidence does not clearly state a specific scientific or public-health implication. Case 3 details an 18-year-old female with a confounding history of hydrocephalus requiring surgical decompression, presenting with scholastic decline, periodic slow-wave discharges, and slow myoclonus.

title: Molecular epidemiology and phylogenetic insights into measles virus in Malaysia, 2018–2024

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles remains a public health concern in Malaysia despite high reported vaccine coverage. This study aimed to characterise the molecular epidemiology of measles virus (MeV) circulating in Malaysia from 2018 to 2024.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 1,110 MeV sequences collected nationwide between 2018 and 2024 from routine surveillance and outbreak investigations were analysed alongside 28 World Health Organization reference strains. The study focused on measles virus sequences and examined vaccination status and demographic metadata to identify epidemiological patterns.
analysis.methods: Partial N-gene (N450) sequences were genotyped using the WHO classification framework. Temporal genotype trends were assessed using logistic regression, genotype distributions were compared using χ2 tests, and phylogenetic analyses were performed using the Nextstrain Augur pipeline.
analysis.main_results: Genotype D8 predominated throughout the study period (94%, n = 1,043), followed by B3 (4%) and genotype A (vaccine-associated) accounted for 2% of detections. Phylogenetic and molecular clock analyses showed that D8 sequences formed a highly conserved lineage (99.2–99.9% nucleotide identity). The odds of D8 detection increased nearly fourfold per year (p < 0.0001). The presence of multiple phylogenetic distinct clusters across the study period was compatible with repeated introductions followed by local amplification.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The observed molecular and phylogenetic patterns were compatible with repeated introductions followed by local amplification, although uninterrupted low-level domestic transmission could not be excluded. The study provided insights into the genetic dynamics of measles virus in Malaysia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of molecular surveillance in understanding measles virus circulation and identifying immunity gaps. They inform public health strategies for measles control and prevention in Malaysia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on routine surveillance data and did not include direct causal evidence. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on sequence analysis and statistical trends without experimental intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the molecular epidemiology of measles virus (MeV) in Malaysia from 2018 to 2024, focusing on genotype D8, which predominated throughout the period. The analysis of 1,110 sequences revealed a highly conserved lineage of D8 with 99.2–99.9% nucleotide identity. The odds of D8 detection increased nearly fourfold per year, suggesting a possible trend in its prevalence. The presence of multiple phylogenetic clusters indicated repeated introductions followed by local amplification, although uninterrupted domestic transmission could not be ruled out. The study underscores the role of molecular surveillance in tracking measles virus circulation and identifying immunity gaps, which has implications for public health strategies in Malaysia. However, the findings are based on sequence data and statistical trends, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: Triple Helix Model for Measles Rubella Vaccine Introduction. Experiences from a National Vaccine Introduction Program

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the practical value of the Triple Helix collaboration model in strengthening measles vaccine uptake and public trust, particularly in addressing vaccine hesitancy and ensuring equitable access.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a national vaccine introduction program in Nigeria, focusing on the planned Measles–Rubella (MR) vaccine rollout in October 2025. It examined the application of a Triple Helix model with stakeholder engagement and structured advocacy as the core methodological approach.
analysis.methods: Stakeholder engagement and structured advocacy were used to facilitate high-level dialogue and demand-generation activities during the Biennial General Conference in Kaduna. Data from the engagement were analysed thematically to distil lessons for collaborative vaccine advocacy.
analysis.main_results: The engagement generated strong intersectoral commitment to a coordinated framework for MR vaccine advocacy, demand generation, and monitoring. Key outcomes included consensus on evidence-based, gender-responsive advocacy strategies and deployment of MWAN’s national and subnational networks for grassroots mobilisation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the practical value of Triple Helix collaboration in strengthening vaccine uptake and public trust. They highlighted the need for deeper university–industry–government partnerships in health innovation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform collaborative vaccine advocacy strategies, demand generation, and monitoring frameworks for measles and rubella vaccination campaigns. They underscore the importance of multi-stakeholder engagement in addressing vaccine hesitancy and ensuring equitable access.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a single event, the Biennial General Conference in Kaduna, and does not include quantitative data or long-term follow-up. The evidence is moderate as it relies on thematic analysis of stakeholder engagement rather than empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the application of a Triple Helix collaboration model in Nigeria's planned Measles–Rubella (MR) vaccine rollout, focusing on addressing vaccine hesitancy and ensuring equitable access. The model involves the Medical Women’s Association of Nigeria (MWAN), the Gates Foundation, and the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA). Stakeholder engagement and structured advocacy were used to facilitate high-level dialogue and demand-generation activities during the Biennial General Conference in Kaduna. Thematic analysis of the engagement data revealed strong intersectoral commitment to a coordinated framework for MR vaccine advocacy, demand generation, and monitoring. The study highlights the practical value of Triple Helix collaboration in strengthening vaccine uptake and public trust, emphasizing the need for deeper university–industry–government partnerships in health innovation. However, the study is limited to a single event and lacks quantitative data or long-term follow-up, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Multi-pathogen serosurveillance reveals correlated vaccination performance, waning tetanus immunity, and diphtheria boosting in Zambian children.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vaccination coverage estimates and case-based surveillance have limitations in evaluating immunization programs. Serosurveillance offers a complementary approach by directly measuring population immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a matched case-control study among children aged 2- to 10-years-old (n = 1286) in Zambia using specimens from the 2016 ZAMPHIA survey.
analysis.methods: Measles seronegative children (i.e., "cases") were matched to measles seropositive children (i.e., "controls") on sex, age, HIV infection status, and province. Samples were tested for tetanus and diphtheria antitoxin IgG antibodies using commercial enzyme immunoassays. We estimated the odds of tetanus and diphtheria seropositivity by measles serostatus using conditional logistic regression and examined age-specific antibody dynamics.
analysis.main_results: Measles seronegative children had 1.7-fold increased odds (95% credible interval [CrI]: 1.3-2.1) of being tetanus seronegative compared to measles seropositive children. Tetanus seroprevalence declined monotonically with age. Diphtheria serostatus had no significant association with measles serostatus (odds ratio: 1.3; 95% CrI: 0.9-1.7).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Serologic analyses revealed measles serostatus was positively associated with tetanus serostatus (where seropositivity arises only via vaccination and not infection), suggesting children who are measles seronegative are more likely to have missed DTP vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: We additionally found that measles serostatus was not associated with diphtheria serostatus, suggesting that antibody responses to diphtheria continue to boost beyond infancy when DTP vaccination is given.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Our findings support consideration of DTP booster doses in Zambia to address waning tetanus immunity and further investigation of potential diphtheria carriage and transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This study used serosurveillance to evaluate vaccination program performance in Zambian children by analyzing measles, tetanus, and diphtheria immunity. The research aimed to determine whether serologic analyses could provide additional insights into immunization effectiveness. A matched case-control study was conducted among 1286 children aged 2- to 10-years-old using specimens from the 2016 ZAMPHIA survey. Measles seronegative children had 1.7-fold increased odds of being tetanus seronegative compared to measles seropositive children, indicating a possible link between measles serostatus and DTP vaccination status. Tetanus seroprevalence decreased with age, while diphtheria serostatus showed no significant association with measles serostatus. The authors suggest that DTP booster doses may be necessary to address waning tetanus immunity and that diphtheria antibody responses may continue to boost beyond infancy. The study highlights the value of serosurveillance in understanding immunization program performance and the dynamics of immunity in children.
